questions.question:
What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '-' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

19 + 55 × 5 - 7 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2042326d26ec7b593e52bbbdd22d890b59b1e59f92be81a7235509e9af1c4625.png] 

Given equation: 19 + 55 × 5 - 7 ÷ 3 = ?

After interchanging ‘+’ and ‘−’ and ‘×’ and ‘÷’, we get:

19 − __**55 ÷ 5**__ + 7 × 3 = ?

= 19 − 11 + __**7 × 3**__

= __**19 − 11**__ + 21

= 8 + 21

= 29

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: The Attorney General of India provides legal advice to _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Attorney General of India is the **chief legal advisor to the Union Government** and is appointed by the President under Article 76 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• He/she represents the Union Government in all legal matters, including cases in the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
• The Attorney General provides legal advice to the government on matters of law and performs any other legal duties assigned by the President.
 
• While the Attorney General has the right to participate in Parliamentary proceedings, he/she does not have voting rights.
 
• The Attorney General must be a person qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court, i.e., with at least 10 years of experience as an advocate or a judge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solicitor General of India**

 
 
• Assists the Attorney General and represents the government in important legal cases.
 
• Unlike the Attorney General, the Solicitor General does not provide advice directly to the government.
 
 
 
• **Advocate General of a State**
 
 
• The Advocate General is the highest legal authority in a state and provides advice to the state government.
 
• He/she is appointed by the Governor under Article 165 of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Role of Attorney General in Constitutional Matters**
 
 
• Acts as an advisor in constitutional disputes and government policies.
 
• Provides guidance on issues like federalism and separation of powers.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of the Attorney General**
 
 
• He/she cannot defend any accused or oppose the government in legal matters.
 
• The Attorney General is not a full-time employee of the government and can take up private legal practice, provided it does not conflict with official duties.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, in which State is the difference in the male and female literacy rates the highest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Census 2011, Rajasthan recorded the **highest difference in male and female literacy rates** among Indian states.
 
• The male literacy rate in Rajasthan was approximately **80.51%**, whereas the female literacy rate stood at **52.66%**, creating a significant gap of **27.85%**.
 
• This disparity highlights **gender inequality** in education, particularly in rural areas of Rajasthan.
 
• Efforts have been made by the state government through programs like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** and Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan to bridge the literacy gap.
 
• Rajasthan has historically faced challenges such as **socio-cultural norms and lack of access to education for women**, contributing to this disparity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate**

 
 
• Literacy rate refers to the percentage of the population aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• It is an essential indicator of a region's social and economic development.
 
 
 
• **Gender Disparity in Literacy**
 
 
• Gender disparity in literacy rates is caused by factors like traditional societal norms, poverty, and lack of access to education.
 
• Government schemes such as **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** aim to reduce this disparity by promoting girl child education.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011**
 
 
• Census 2011 is the 15th Indian Census conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on population, literacy rates, employment, and housing conditions.
 
 
 
• **Schemes to Promote Literacy**
 
 
• **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan:** Focuses on universal access to education and improving literacy rates.
 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao:** Aims to improve gender equality in education and combat discrimination against girls.

questions.question: According to the Vishnu Purana, who was Chandragupta Maurya's mother?

options.text: The wife of a Nanda king

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mura, daughter of a hunter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Vishnu Purana, Chandragupta Maurya’s mother was **Mura**, who was described as the daughter of a hunter.
 
• Mura is often referred to as a woman of humble origin, whose lineage was tied to the **Shudra class**.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power is frequently cited as an example of how individuals from lower social strata could ascend to great heights in ancient India.
 
• Historical texts and puranas emphasize Chandragupta's humble beginnings, which contributed to his perception as a transformative leader.
 
• The Vishnu Purana, along with other ancient texts like the Buddhist chronicles, provides various accounts of Chandragupta’s ancestry, reflecting the diverse narratives surrounding his life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• He was the founder of the Maurya Empire, which became one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• Chandragupta was guided by his mentor, Chanakya, who authored the **Arthashastra**, a treatise on governance and economics.
 
• Under his reign, the Maurya Empire unified the Indian subcontinent and established a centralized administration.
 
• Chandragupta later renounced his throne and adopted Jainism, spending his final years as an ascetic.
 
 
 
• **Vishnu Purana:**
 
 
• It is one of the eighteen Mahapuranas, a genre of ancient Indian texts.
 
• The Vishnu Purana provides genealogies of kings and stories of prominent figures like Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The Purana emphasizes the role of Vishnu in preserving dharma and cosmic order.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya’s Role:**
 
 
• Chanakya, also known as Kautilya, was the political advisor and strategist behind Chandragupta’s success.
 
• He played a pivotal role in overthrowing the Nanda dynasty and establishing the Maurya Empire.
 
• Chanakya’s teachings in the Arthashastra include principles of governance, economics, and military strategy.
 
 
 
• **Social Stratification in Ancient India:**
 
 
• Ancient Indian society was divided into varnas (social classes), with Shudras typically occupying the lowest tier.
 
• Chandragupta’s ascent challenged traditional notions of caste-based hierarchies.

questions.question: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister, approved which scheme to promote sustainable agriculture and to achieve food security for self sufficiency in October 2024?

options.text: National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology
National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **PM Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)** aims to achieve food security, sustainable agriculture, and self-sufficiency by promoting growth in the agricultural sector.
 
• It is a state plan scheme launched in 2007 but restructured as **RKVY-Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation (RKVY-RAFTAAR)** in 2017 to focus on pre- and post-harvest infrastructure.
 
• Under this scheme, funds are provided to states as grants for agricultural development, ensuring decentralization and flexibility for local needs.
 
• The scheme also supports innovation and technology adoption in agriculture to increase productivity and profitability for farmers.
 
• It aligns with the government's goal of doubling farmers' incomes by 2024, with a focus on value addition, market linkages, and sustainable farming practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Agriculture**

 
 
• It involves practices that maintain soil health, conserve water, and reduce dependency on chemical inputs.
 
• Techniques include crop rotation, organic farming, integrated pest management, and agroforestry.
 
• Sustainable agriculture ensures long-term productivity while minimizing environmental harm.
 
 
 
• **National Food Security Mission (NFSM)**
 
 
• Launched in 2007-08, it aims to increase the production of rice, wheat, pulses, and coarse cereals to meet the growing demand.
 
• It focuses on area expansion, productivity enhancement, and restoring soil fertility.
 
• The mission operates through cluster demonstrations, distribution of quality seeds, and resource conservation technologies.
 
 
 
• **National Mission on Oilseeds and Oil Palm (NMOOP)**
 
 
• It was launched in 2014-15 to augment the production of edible oils by promoting oilseeds and oil palm cultivation.
 
• The mission aims to achieve self-sufficiency in edible oil production and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• It emphasizes increasing the area under cultivation, improving productivity, and adopting high-yielding varieties.
 
 
 
• **Krishi Infrastructure Fund**
 
 
• Launched in 2020, it provides financial support for building post-harvest infrastructure and community farming assets.
 
• The fund has a corpus of Rs. 1 lakh crore, focusing on storage, processing, and value-addition facilities.
 
• It empowers farmers and Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) to gain better market access and reduce wastage.

The correct answer is __**Folk Music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Padmashree Mukund Nayak is a celebrated folk artist from Jharkhand, known for his contributions to the **folk music traditions of the state**.
 
• He was honoured with the prestigious **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** in 2017 for his exceptional contributions to **folk music**.
 
• The award is India’s highest recognition given to practicing artists for their outstanding work in various performing arts categories, including music, dance, and theater.
 
• Mukund Nayak has worked extensively to preserve and promote the **Karma folk tradition**, a cultural heritage of Jharkhand.
 
• His efforts in bringing Jharkhand's folk music to national recognition have greatly contributed to the preservation of indigenous art forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards:**

 
 
• Established in 1952, these awards are conferred annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• The awards recognize outstanding achievements in various performing arts categories such as classical music, folk music, dance, and theater.
 
• Recipients receive a cash prize, a citation, and a tamrapatra (copper plaque).
 
 
 
• **Karma Folk Tradition:**
 
 
• Karma is a popular folk dance and music tradition practiced predominantly in Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It celebrates nature and the harvest season, performed during the Karma festival.
 
• The music involves traditional instruments like the mandar, nagara, and flute.
 
 
 
• **Padmashree Award:**
 
 
• It is the fourth highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contributions in various fields such as art, literature, education, sports, and social service.
 
• Mukund Nayak was awarded the Padmashree for his contributions to folk music and cultural preservation.
 
 
 
• **Preservation of Folk Music:**
 
 
• Folk music reflects the cultural heritage and traditions of a region, passed down orally through generations.
 
• Efforts to preserve folk music include documentation, performances, and integration into mainstream platforms.
 
• Artists like Mukund Nayak play a crucial role in safeguarding these traditions against the rapid modernization of society.

questions.question: In which month does the Rann Utsav start at Kachchh, Gujarat?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Rann Utsav** is an annual cultural festival celebrated in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
 
• It begins in the month of **November** and continues until February, showcasing the vibrant culture, crafts, and traditions of Gujarat.
 
• The festival is organized by the Gujarat Tourism Department and attracts tourists from across the globe.
 
• Key attractions include the **white salt desert**, folk music and dance performances, camel rides, adventure sports, and traditional Gujarati cuisine.
 
• The event is held in Dhordo village, often referred to as the **"Tent City"** due to its luxurious tent accommodations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rann of Kutch**

 
 
• The Rann of Kutch is a seasonal salt marsh located in the Thar Desert in Gujarat.
 
• It spans an area of approximately 7,500 square kilometers, making it one of the largest salt deserts in the world.
 
• The region is known for its unique geography, biodiversity, and cultural significance.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Rann Utsav**
 
 
• The festival highlights the art, craft, and cultural heritage of Gujarat.
 
• It boosts tourism and contributes significantly to the local economy.
 
• It provides a platform for artisans and performers to showcase their talent and promote indigenous crafts.
 
 
 
• **Activities at Rann Utsav**
 
 
• Adventure activities such as paramotoring, ATV rides, and hot air ballooning are popular among visitors.
 
• Shopping for handmade crafts, jewelry, and textiles is a key attraction.
 
• Visitors can enjoy stargazing, as the desert offers clear night skies.

• The ideal time to attend Rann Utsav is between November and February when the weather is pleasant.
 
• The full moon nights during the festival offer breathtaking views of the white desert illuminated by moonlight.

questions.question: What was the pre-determined principle announced in the Union Budget for 2018-19 regarding the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for the principal crops in India?

options.text: Equal to the cost of production
One-and-a-half times the cost of production
50 per cent less than the cost of production

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-and-a-half times the cost of production**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In the Union Budget for 2018-19, the government announced that the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for all principal crops would be set at **one-and-a-half times (1.5x) the cost of production**.
 
• This decision aimed to ensure remunerative prices for farmers and address the issue of agrarian distress in the country.
 
• The MSP calculation is based on the comprehensive cost of production, including expenses such as seeds, fertilizers, labor, irrigation, and other inputs.
 
• The announcement was in line with the Swaminathan Commission's recommendations, which advocated fixing MSP at least 50% higher than the cost of production.
 
• The initiative was primarily targeted at improving farmers' income and boosting agricultural productivity in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minimum Support Price (MSP):**

 
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the Government of India to safeguard farmers against sharp price falls during bumper production years.
 
• The MSP is announced for 22 mandated crops and is determined by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).
 
• It is based on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP).
 
 
 
• **Swaminathan Commission:**
 
 
• The National Commission on Farmers, chaired by Dr. M.S. Swaminathan, recommended fixing MSP at least 50% above the cost of production (C2).
 
• The formula includes both input costs (A2) and the imputed value of family labor (FL).
 
 
 
• **Types of Costs in MSP Calculation:**
 
 
• **A2:** Includes out-of-pocket expenses like seeds, fertilizers, and labor.
 
• **A2+FL:** A2 costs plus the imputed value of unpaid family labor.
 
• **C2:** Comprehensive cost, including A2+FL and the rental value of owned land and interest on fixed capital.
 
 
 
• **Implementation and Benefits:**
 
 
• The 1.5x MSP policy ensures better income for farmers and reduces their dependence on informal credit systems.
 
• It also incentivizes crop diversification and adoption of sustainable farming practices.

questions.question: When was the First Five-Year Plan launched in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The First Five-Year Plan of India was launched in **1951** and covered the period from 1951 to 1956.
 
• It was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model**, which emphasized investment and savings as the key to economic growth.
 
• The primary focus of the First Five-Year Plan was on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy** to address food shortages and boost rural development.
 
• The plan aimed at achieving a growth rate of **2.1%** annually, but India successfully achieved a growth rate of around **3.6%**.
 
• The Planning Commission, established in **1950**, was responsible for formulating and overseeing the implementation of the Five-Year Plans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• India adopted the concept of centralized economic planning inspired by the Soviet Union.
 
• The Planning Commission was established under the leadership of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru** to implement the Five-Year Plans.
 
• Each plan targeted specific sectors such as agriculture, industry, and social development based on national priorities.
 
• The Five-Year Plans continued until **2017**, when they were replaced by the **NITI Aayog's Three-Year Action Agenda**.
 
 
 
• **Harrod-Domar Model**
 
 
• This economic model emphasizes the importance of savings and investment in achieving economic growth.
 
• The model assumes that economic growth is directly proportional to the savings rate and inversely proportional to the capital-output ratio.
 
• It was used as a foundational framework for India's First Five-Year Plan.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission**
 
 
• Established in **1950**, the Planning Commission was tasked with assessing resources and formulating India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• The commission worked under the chairmanship of the Prime Minister and included experts from various fields.
 
• It was replaced by **NITI Aayog** in **2015** to better align with contemporary needs.
 
 
 
• **Focus of the First Five-Year Plan**
 
 
• The plan prioritized **agriculture** due to severe food shortages in the post-independence period.
 
• Key projects included the development of irrigation systems like the **Bhakra Nangal Dam** and energy initiatives.
 
• It also focused on land reforms and rural development to improve livelihoods in the countryside.

questions.question: In which sport does the "Timed Out" rule apply?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Timed Out" rule in cricket is outlined in the **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) Laws of Cricket**, under Law 40.
 
• This rule states that a new batter must be ready to face the next delivery or at the crease within **three minutes** of the previous batter's dismissal.
 
• If the incoming batter fails to arrive within the stipulated time, the fielding team can appeal to the umpire to declare the batter as "Timed Out."
 
• The "Timed Out" rule is a rare mode of dismissal and emphasizes maintaining the pace and flow of the game.
 
• This rule applies to all formats of cricket, including **Test matches, One-Day Internationals (ODIs), and Twenty20 (T20) matches**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rare Dismissal Modes in Cricket:**

 
 
• Other rare modes of dismissal in cricket include **Hit Wicket**, **Obstructing the Field**, **Handling the Ball** (now included under Obstructing the Field), and **Retired Out**.
 
• These dismissals occur infrequently in professional matches compared to common methods like bowled, caught, or LBW.
 
 
 
• **Historical Instances of Timed Out:**
 
 
• The first recorded instance of a "Timed Out" dismissal in first-class cricket occurred in 1987 when Andrew Jordaan was dismissed in South Africa's domestic competition.
 
• There have been very few instances of this dismissal in professional cricket, making it one of the rarest ways to lose a wicket.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Rule:**
 
 
• The rule ensures that the game maintains its rhythm and prevents unnecessary delays caused by players taking excessive time to get ready.
 
• It also serves to uphold the spirit of the game by emphasizing punctuality and readiness among players.
 
 
 
• **Recent Updates to MCC Laws:**
 
 
• The MCC regularly updates the Laws of Cricket to address evolving scenarios and ensure fairness in the game.
 
• The 2022 Code of Laws included revisions to clarify several rules, including "Timed Out," to ensure better understanding and implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following was a new agricultural practice introduced during the Green Revolution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Use of modern irrigation techniques**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution introduced advanced agricultural practices, including the use of **modern irrigation techniques** like drip and sprinkler systems for water conservation.
 
• Modern irrigation methods ensured **efficient utilization of water resources** and helped increase crop yields, especially in areas with scarce water supply.
 
• These techniques supported the cultivation of high-yield variety (HYV) crops, which required **timely and adequate water supply** for optimal growth.
 
• The adoption of modern irrigation systems reduced dependency on **monsoon rainfall**, making agriculture more resilient to climate variability.
 
• Modern irrigation played a critical role in transforming India’s agricultural sector during the Green Revolution, contributing to **food security and self-sufficiency**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yield Variety (HYV) Seeds:**

 
 
• HYV seeds were developed to produce higher output per hectare compared to traditional seeds.
 
• These seeds often required proper irrigation, fertilizers, and pesticides for maximum productivity.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution encouraged the use of chemical fertilizers to enhance soil fertility and crop production.
 
• Pesticides were introduced to protect crops from pests and diseases, ensuring a more stable yield.
 
 
 
• **Mechanization of Agriculture:**
 
 
• Tractors, harvesters, and other machinery replaced traditional animal labor, significantly improving efficiency.
 
• Mechanization allowed large-scale farming and reduced manual labor dependency.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Food Security:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution helped India achieve self-sufficiency in food grains, reducing dependency on imports.
 
• It significantly contributed to reducing hunger and malnutrition in the country.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Excessive use of fertilizers and pesticides caused soil degradation and water pollution.
 
• Modern irrigation techniques, though efficient, sometimes led to waterlogging and salinization in certain areas.

questions.question: The increased concentration of suspended solids in water and their accumulation on bottoms where they are undesirable, creates what kind of water pollution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Siltation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Siltation** refers to the process by which fine particles like silt and sediment accumulate in water bodies, leading to pollution and degradation of aquatic ecosystems.
 
• This type of pollution occurs due to activities like **deforestation, mining, and construction** that increase erosion and sediment runoff.
 
• Siltation can disrupt aquatic habitats by **blocking sunlight penetration**, reducing oxygen levels, and smothering organisms living on the seabed or riverbed.
 
• It also affects water quality and can **reduce the capacity of reservoirs, lakes, and rivers**, impacting human activities such as irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• Preventive measures include **soil conservation practices**, afforestation, and the use of sediment control techniques to reduce erosion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Suspended solids:**

 
 
• They are small solid particles that remain in water due to turbulence or slow settling rates.
 
• Sources include agricultural runoff, industrial discharge, and urban stormwater.
 
• Excessive suspended solids can lead to turbidity, reducing light penetration and affecting aquatic photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Impact of siltation:**
 
 
• Damages aquatic ecosystems by burying habitats and reducing biodiversity.
 
• Causes economic losses by reducing the efficiency of water infrastructure such as reservoirs and dams.
 
• Can lead to increased flooding due to reduced channel capacity.
 
 
 
• **Soil erosion:**
 
 
• A major contributor to siltation, caused by deforestation, overgrazing, and improper land management.
 
• Erosion control measures include terracing, planting vegetation, and using sediment barriers.
 
 
 
• **Other types of water pollution:**
 
 
• **Thermal pollution:** Caused by the discharge of heated water, impacting aquatic life.
 
• **Microbiological pollution:** Involves harmful pathogens entering water, affecting human and animal health.
 
• **Nutrient pollution:** Excess nitrogen and phosphorus lead to eutrophication, depleting oxygen levels in water bodies.

questions.question: Which law is Willebrod Snell's most important contribution to science?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Law of Refraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Willebrord Snell, a Dutch mathematician and astronomer, formulated the **Law of Refraction**, commonly known as Snell's Law, in 1621.
 
• **Snell's Law** mathematically describes how light bends when it passes from one medium to another with different refractive indices.
 
• The law is expressed as **n₁sinθ₁ = n₂sinθ₂**, where n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction respectively.
 
• This discovery is fundamental to the field of optics and is widely used in designing lenses, optical instruments, and understanding light behavior.
 
• The law also underpins modern technologies such as fiber optics, laser systems, and imaging devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction:**

 
 
• Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium to another due to a change in its speed.
 
• It is governed by the refractive index, which is a measure of how much light slows down in a medium compared to a vacuum.
 
• Applications include magnifying glasses, cameras, telescopes, and corrective lenses.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:**
 
 
• The refractive index is a dimensionless number indicating the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum to its speed in a given medium.
 
• It determines how much light will bend when transitioning between materials.
 
• Common values: Air (≈1), Water (≈1.33), Glass (≈1.5).
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle and Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• The critical angle is the angle of incidence above which light is entirely reflected within a medium, rather than refracted.
 
• Total internal reflection is a phenomenon used in fiber optics and diamond brilliance.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Fiber optic communication systems rely on controlled refraction and total internal reflection.
 
• It is essential in lens design for cameras, microscopes, and telescopes.
 
• Understanding atmospheric refraction helps explain phenomena like mirages and the apparent bending of starlight.

questions.question: Which of the following generally form at the upper part of a river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gorges**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gorges** are deep, narrow valleys with steep sides, typically formed by the erosional activity of a river in its upper course.
 
• These are created due to the river cutting vertically into the bedrock as it flows downhill with high energy, carving out steep walls over time.
 
• Gorges are most commonly formed in areas with resistant rock, where the river's erosive power is greater than the resistance of the rock.
 
• The formation of a gorge is a characteristic feature of a river's youthful stage, where it flows rapidly down steep gradients.
 
• Examples include the Kali Gandaki Gorge in Nepal and the Grand Canyon in the USA, both of which highlight the erosive power of rivers over millennia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Upper Course of a River:**

 
 
• It is the first stage of a river’s journey, typically found in mountainous or hilly regions.
 
• Rivers in this stage have high velocity and energy, leading to vertical erosion and the formation of features like gorges, waterfalls, and rapids.
 
 
 
• **Other Features of a River's Upper Course:**
 
 
• **Waterfalls:** Sudden drops in a river's course, often formed where hard rock overlays softer rock.
 
• **Rapids:** Sections of turbulent, fast-flowing water caused by a steep gradient or obstacles in the riverbed.
 
 
 
• **Meanders and Floodplains:**
 
 
• These are features of the river's middle and lower courses where the flow is slower, and lateral erosion and deposition dominate.
 
• Unlike gorges, meanders and floodplains are absent in the upper course due to high energy and steep gradients.
 
 
 
• **Oxbow Lakes:**
 
 
• These are U-shaped water bodies formed from abandoned meanders in the lower course of a river.
 
• Their formation occurs due to sediment deposition cutting off a meander loop from the main river channel.

questions.question: Which classical dance form originated in Kuchelapuram village of Krishna district?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kuchipudi** is a classical dance form originating from **Kuchelapuram village** in Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• It was developed as a form of **dance-drama** combining music, acting, and movement, which is unique among Indian classical dance forms.
 
• The dance form is named after its place of origin, **Kuchelapuram**, and traditionally performed by male Brahmin priests.
 
• Kuchipudi performances often depict stories from Hindu mythology, especially the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.
 
• Over time, Kuchipudi transitioned into a refined classical art form, incorporating **intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive storytelling.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin and Development:**

 
 
• Kuchipudi originated in the 3rd century BCE, but its codified form emerged in the 17th century under Siddhendra Yogi.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi is considered the father of Kuchipudi and refined it into a structured art form.
 
 
 
• **Performance Style:**
 
 
• It is characterized by rapid footwork, dramatic expression, and rhythmic patterns.
 
• Performers often combine singing and acting with dancing, making it a holistic art form.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Makeup:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi dancers wear vibrant costumes, intricate jewelry, and expressive makeup to enhance their storytelling.
 
• The attire varies based on the character being portrayed, such as gods, demons, or humans.
 
 
 
• **Modern Adaptations:**
 
 
• While Kuchipudi was historically performed by men, today, women also actively participate and dominate the art form.
 
• Contemporary Kuchipudi performances often include solo dances, which were rare in traditional formats.

questions.question: The Government of India Act, 1935 provided for how many lists of divisions of power between the federation (central government) and provinces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced a federal structure with a division of powers between the central government (federation) and provinces through **three legislative lists**.
 
• The three lists were categorized as **Federal List**, **Provincial List**, and **Concurrent List**.
 
• **Federal List** included subjects under the exclusive jurisdiction of the central government such as defense, foreign affairs, and railways.
 
• **Provincial List** contained subjects under the provincial governments, including police, public health, and education.
 
• **Concurrent List** covered subjects where both the center and provinces could legislate, such as criminal law and marriage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1935:**

 
 
• It was the longest and most detailed legislation ever passed by the British Parliament for India.
 
• The Act introduced provincial autonomy, allowing provinces to function as autonomous administrative units.
 
• It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court to resolve disputes between provinces and the federation.
 
• The Act also proposed the creation of an All-India Federation, but it never came into effect due to lack of agreement among princely states.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The concept of a concurrent list was introduced for the first time in Indian legislative history by the 1935 Act.
 
• It laid the foundation for cooperative federalism in India, later adopted in the Constitution of India (1950).
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1935 served as an important blueprint for the drafting of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Many features such as division of powers, bicameralism, and federal structure were adopted and refined in the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Federalism:** A system of governance where power is divided between central and regional authorities.
 
• **Provincial Autonomy:** The ability of provinces to govern themselves independently within certain areas.

questions.question: What is the standard width of the field in an international hockey match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**55 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The standard width of a hockey field for international matches is **55 meters**, as per the regulations set by the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
 
• The field is rectangular, with a length of **91.4 meters** and a width of **55 meters**, ensuring uniformity in competitive play.
 
• The field is divided into halves, each featuring a **23-meter line** that helps demarcate key playing zones.
 
• The dimensions are strictly maintained to support fair gameplay and adherence to international standards.
 
• The goalposts are placed at the center of each width side, with standardized dimensions to align with the field size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Field Markings:**

 
 
• The field includes distinct markings such as the **23-meter line, penalty spot, and shooting circle**.
 
• The shooting circle is a **D-shaped area** around the goal, where attacking players can score.
 
 
 
• **Surface Type:**
 
 
• International hockey matches are generally played on **synthetic turf**, which ensures consistent ball movement and player traction.
 
• Natural grass was traditionally used but is now rare due to maintenance challenges and uneven play.
 
 
 
• **Goal Dimensions:**
 
 
• The goal width is **3.66 meters**, and the height is **2.14 meters**, standardized for all international matches.
 
• The goalposts are equipped with nets to catch the ball securely after scoring.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Body:**
 
 
• The **International Hockey Federation (FIH)** is responsible for setting and enforcing field dimensions and other rules globally.
 
• FIH regulations ensure uniform standards across international tournaments.

questions.question: The Quit India Resolution was passed during which session of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Session**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Quit India Resolution was passed during the **Bombay Session of the Indian National Congress** held on **8 August 1942**.
 
• This session was presided over by **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, who was the President of the Indian National Congress at the time.
 
• The resolution, also known as the **"August Kranti"**, marked the beginning of the Quit India Movement against British rule in India.
 
• The movement called for immediate independence of India and was characterized by the slogan **"Do or Die"**, given by Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• The British government reacted swiftly by arresting top Congress leaders, including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel, effectively crippling the movement's leadership.

questions.question: The population of a district is 369000, out of which 186000 are males. 45% of the population is literate. If 45% males are literate, then what percentage of females are literate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the rule of weighted averages, if an overall group is divided into subgroups, the overall percentage is the weighted average of the subgroup percentages.

Overall district literacy rate = 45%

Male literacy rate = 45%

Since the male literacy rate is exactly equal to the overall literacy rate, the female literacy rate must also be equal to the overall literacy rate to balance the average.

**∴ The correct answer is 45%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Population Literacy Distribution
 
 
 
 Total: 369000 | Literate: 45%

 Males: 186000
 Females: 183000

 
 
 Lit: 45%

 
 
 Lit: ? = 45%

 
 Literate Population

**Given:**

Total population = 369000

Number of males = 186000

Overall literate population = 45% of total

Literate males = 45% of total males

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of females = Total population − Number of males

⇒ Number of females = 369000 − 186000 = 183000

⇒ Total literate population = Literate males + Literate females

⇒ Literate females = Total literate population − Literate males

⇒ Literate females = (45% of 369000) − (45% of 186000)

⇒ Taking 45% common: Literate females = 45% of (369000 − 186000)

⇒ Literate females = 45% of 183000

⇒ Percentage of literate females = (Literate females ÷ Total females) × 100

⇒ Percentage of literate females = [(45% of 183000) ÷ 183000] × 100

⇒ Percentage of literate females = 45%

**∴ The correct answer is 45%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Rule

If a group is divided into two mutually exclusive subsets and one subset has the exact same average or percentage as the entire combined group, the remaining subset will necessarily also share the exact same average or percentage. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Distributive Property in Percentages

Calculating percentages separately and then subtracting is mathematically identical to finding the percentage of the difference directly: x% of A − x% of B = x% of (A − B). Applying this rule eliminates the need to calculate excessively large raw numerical values during the exam.

questions.question: Amit invests a sum of ₹5400 and Gopal invests a sum of ₹9400 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 6 years, Gopal gets ₹960 more interest than Amit, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹9400 − ₹5400 = ₹4000

Difference in Interest = ₹960, Time = 6 years

Rate (R) = (Difference in Interest × 100) ÷ (Difference in Principal × Time)

R = (960 × 100) ÷ (4000 × 6) = 96000 ÷ 24000

R = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amit's Principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Gopal's Principal (P₂) = ₹9400

Time (T) = 6 years

Difference in Interest = ₹960

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Amit: P = ₹5400
 
 
 Gopal: P = ₹5400
 
 
 + ₹4000 Extra

 

 Generates ₹960 SI in 6 yrs

 Rate = R% (Same for both)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Gopal's SI − Amit's SI = 960

⇒ [(9400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] − [(5400 × R × 6) ÷ 100] = 960

⇒ 564R − 324R = 960

⇒ 240R = 960

⇒ R = 960 ÷ 240

⇒ R = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate of Interest, and T is Time period.

Difference in Simple Interest

When the rate and time are constant, the difference in simple interest earned is directly proportional to the difference in the principal amounts: ΔI = (ΔP × R × T) ÷ 100.

Amount Formula

The total amount (A) at the end of the time period is the sum of the principal and the simple interest: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

questions.question: The price of a shirt is first increased by 15% and then decreased by 12%, and again increased by 8%. Find the net increase or decrease percentage (correct to one decimal place) in the price of the shirt.

Use the successive percentage change formula for two values: a + b + (a × b)/100

Combine the first two changes (+15% and −12%):

⇒ 15 − 12 − (15 × 12)/100 = 3 − 1.8 = +1.2%

Now combine this result with the third change (+1.2% and +8%):

⇒ 1.2 + 8 + (1.2 × 8)/100 = 9.2 + 0.096 = +9.296%

⇒ Rounding to one decimal place, the net change is +9.3%.

**∴ The correct answer is Increase of 9.3%.**

⇒ Price after 2nd change (12% decrease) = 115 × (88/100) = 101.2

Successive Percentage Formula

For two consecutive changes of a% and b%, the combined effect is calculated as (a + b + ab/100)%. Use positive signs for increases and negative signs for decreases.

Fractional Ratio Method

When dealing with fractional percentages like 16.66% or 14.28%, convert them into fractions first. The successive change is calculated directly by multiplying the initial base ratio parts and comparing with the final ratio parts.

Effective Discount

A series of discounts d₁% and d₂% is equivalent to a single net discount of (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%. It's a special case of successive percentage where values strictly decrease.
